claims.text: The additive-manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA contains dual, well-distributed nanoprecipitates in a solid-solution matrix.
In situ high-temperature TEM combined with real-time EDS can reveal elemental redistribution within the nanoprecipitates during oxidation.
In situ characterization can resolve time- and temperature-dependent changes occurring during HEA oxidation.
Controlled high-temperature oxidation causes significant elemental redistribution within the nanoprecipitates of Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3.
Nanoprecipitate elemental redistribution modulates formation of the oxide scale.
Nanoprecipitate elemental redistribution modulates the protective quality of the oxide scale.
The oxidation experiment can regulate temperature and oxygen partial pressure.
The proposed elevated-temperature oxygen environments simulate gas-turbine or aerospace service conditions.
At high temperatures, nanoprecipitates undergo elemental diffusion and redistribution.
Elemental redistribution changes local surface chemistry and thereby drives formation and stability of protective oxide layers.
Real-time EDS will show time-dependent changes in nanoprecipitate composition.
Changes in nanoprecipitate composition will correlate with changes in oxide-scale morphology.
Changes in nanoprecipitate composition will correlate with changes in the protective characteristics of the oxide scale.
Traditional post-mortem characterization does not capture temporal dynamics of elemental redistribution.
The proposed mechanism is restricted to high-temperature oxidative environments and may not apply at low temperature or under non-oxidative conditions.
